figures.caption: Core classes: module and tracking
figures.heading: Core: the module and train tracking
figures.note: - StubCtcOffice implements CtcOffice. It holds the orders, closures, switch commands and granted blocks, and owns one TrackGraph per line, the TrainTracker and, once a schedule is loaded, the AutoDispatcher. - _Layout checks every reference and input against the layout files. - Every refusal is a CtcError: InvalidInputError (bad value), InvalidTimeStepError, MaintenanceModeRequiredError, UnsafeActionError (a safety rule). - TrainTracker keeps one Tracked per train: its blocks, how far it may have got, the fastest it may be going and the block it came from. Each step it reads the last step's Plan per train and the trains released (Waiting).

figures.caption: Core classes: scheduling, routing and data
figures.heading: Core: scheduling, routing and data
figures.note: - plan_run turns each ScheduledTrain into a RunPlan: its stops in track order with due times, the path out and back, and where on it each stop is. - AutoDispatcher keeps a Progress per run and the two-way zones per line. Each step it reads a World and gives Order and Cancel actions, which the model carries out with the dispatcher's own safety checks. - TrackGraph is built from a Line's blocks; authority() counts an AuthorityLimit along a route.

figures.caption: CTC Office: boundary types
figures.heading: Boundary types
figures.note: All are frozen dataclasses in ctc/interface.py, owned by the CTC Office (D005); other modules' types never appear in them, and common/interfaces.py is not used (D008). CtcSnapshot is for the CTC window only and crosses no module boundary.

figures.caption: Process and window classes
figures.heading: Process and window classes
figures.note: - CtcOfficeProcess answers the harness through ModuleLink and steps the module through CtcHost. - CtcHost is the only object QML talks to: it reads snapshots into rows, and its slots return an empty string or the refusal's text. - HarnessClockBridge gives QML the same clock face as the standalone clock, but shows the harness's time, and hands Run, Pause and 1x / 10x to the module and the harness.

figures.caption: Core classes
figures.heading: Core classes
figures.note: - SwTrackController holds one _Wayside per wayside of every loaded line, and scans each once per step. While any wayside of a line has no program, every wayside of that line idles. - TrackController is one wayside. - It owns its territory (ControllerConfig, Blocks), its ControllerInputs, the user's Program, and the compiled vital Program. - scan decodes the inputs, runs both programs and encodes the OUT_ bits into ControllerOutputs. - run_program does the same on a copy of the inputs (UC-05). - commit installs a program as a new Iteration, keeping the last five. - Program is immutable: a compiled program never changes while it is scanned. diagnostics lists any problems; any diagnostic blocks a commit.

figures.caption: Track layout
figures.heading: Track layout
figures.note: - layout.parse_layout reads the course layout into a ParsedLayout. - build_line divides its blocks among the fixed number of waysides (WAYSIDE_COUNTS) into ControllerConfigs, so that every switch lies inside one wayside. - Switch, WaysideSignal and Crossing name their PLC outputs (SW_s, SIG_s_*, XING_c).

figures.caption: Track Controller (SW): boundary types
figures.heading: Boundary types
figures.note: - All the boundary types are frozen dataclasses. - Every block is named by BlockKey(line, block_id). A switch, its signal and a crossing are named by the block they sit on. - Speeds are whole m/s; authorities are block counts (D013). - TrackControllerOutputs.ready is derived from the per-wayside CtcReports.

figures.caption: Host-side classes
figures.heading: Host-side classes
figures.note: - TrackControllerState is the only object QML talks to. It owns the SwTrackController, holds the editor buffer and its last clean run, and pushes rows into BlockListModel, which updates in place. - StimulusServer accepts one test client at a time on a named pipe. It runs step, user (a window action), clock and hello messages against TrackControllerState. - TestClientState runs in the test UI process. - Its StandInWorld plays the CTC Office and the Track Model, moving simple Trains block by block. - Its ClockDriver plays the shared clock.

figures.caption: Core classes: control
figures.heading: Core classes (Raspberry Pi)
figures.note: - HwTrackController holds one Wayside per loaded database, all on one line, and scans each once per step. While any wayside is not ready, every wayside holds fail-safe. - Wayside owns its territory, the user's Program, and (planned) the generated vital Program. scan builds the input image, runs the programs on both channels, compares them, drives the outputs and builds the CtcReport. - Program is immutable: a compiled program never changes while it is scanned. Each Statement carries a tree (channel A) and postfix code (channel B). - On the Pi, PiLinkServer (common/hw_link/agent.py) reads requests from the USB gadget serial port, journals them, and passes them to TrackCore, which steps the controller, runs the allowlisted window actions (load_territory, load_program, reset) and packs snapshots for the window.

figures.caption: Host-side classes: presentation
figures.heading: Host-side classes (PC)
figures.note: - TrackControllerState is the only object QML talks to. It reads a snapshot, turns it into rows through views, and pushes them into five RowsModels that update in place. - RemoteTrackController (common/hw_link/remote_track.py) implements the same Protocol as HwTrackController, so the window is unchanged. It caches the snapshot the Pi pushes and turns each window action into one request through HardwareRelay; errors come back typed. - ModuleLink answers the harness: each STEP goes to HardwareRelay.submit_step, and the Pi's reply comes back as OUTPUTS or REJECTED. HardwareRelay keeps requests in order, holds replies while the USB link is lost, and SerialTransport finds the Pi by its USB identity.
